label: Early-sequence first-occurrence of <DEL>/u/2/k/q/n/g/e (diffuse)
explanation: Fires during the original-input phase and on the delimiter, almost never in the copy phase (5% of mass). It never fires at t=0 and rarely at t=1; the rate peaks at t=3-4 and falls off for later positions and longer sequences. <DEL> is the strongest single input (22% rate, 37% of mass), followed by u (21%) and then 2/k/q/n/g/e (~7-11%). It fires mostly on first occurrences of a token (94% of mass) and barely on repeats. Magnitude is higher when the earliest tokens are d, i, r (also 0/c/y/x/s): the top activations (~0.39) are <DEL> or u at t=3 after prefixes like "d d f" or "i r d". Requiring an earlier d/r/i/0/c/y/x/s raises F1 only from 0.36 to 0.42. The predicate covers about 80% of activation mass, but precision is low (~0.24): most early first-occurrence steps with these inputs stay below threshold, so the neuron looks like a diffuse readout of the early-prefix hidden state rather than a clean token or position detector. Does not fire in the copy phase, at t=0, or on repeated tokens.
